'''Alexa S. Beiser''' is an American professor of biostatistics and public health researcher. 

==Biography==
Beiser did her PhD in mathematics at Boston University, following her M.A. at the [[University of California, San Diego]] in Applied Mathematics and B.A. in Biology and Psychology from the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bu.edu/sph/profile/alexa-beiser/|title=Alexa Beiser &#124; SPH|website=www.bu.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bumc.bu.edu/busm/profile/alexa-beiser/|title=Alexa Beiser &#124; School of Medicine|website=www.bumc.bu.edu}}</ref>

She has worked at the [[Boston University School of Public Health]] since 1985, currently in the [[Framingham Heart Study]] (FHS) neurology group. Beiser co-developed the biostatistics doctoral program at [[Boston University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alexa Beiser {{!}} SPH |url=https://www.bu.edu/sph/profile/alexa-beiser/ |access-date=2022-08-14 |website=www.bu.edu}}</ref>

==Research==
She has worked on areas such as risk factors for [[dementia]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bu.edu/sph/news/articles/2017/dementia-studies-indicate-rates-are-leveling-off-despite-aging-population/|title=Dementia Rates Leveling Off, Despite Aging Population &#124; SPH|website=www.bu.edu}}</ref> how stress affects memory,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bu.edu/sph/news/articles/2018/stress-associated-with-impaired-memory-lower-brain-volumes/|title=Stress Associated with Impaired Memory, Lower Brain Volumes &#124; SPH|website=www.bu.edu}}</ref> and how physical activity can improve health for people with diabetes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bu.edu/sph/news/articles/2019/physical-activity-improves-cognitive-and-vascular-health-in-older-people-with-diabetes/|title=Physical Activity Improves Cognitive and Vascular Health in Older People with Diabetes &#124; SPH|website=www.bu.edu}}</ref> She currently leads the FHS neurology group data management team, with a focus of analysing data relating to dementia.

==Selected papers==

*Plasma Homocysteine as a Risk Factor for Dementia and Alzheimer's Disease, N Engl J Med 2002; 346:476-483, {{doi|10.1056/NEJMoa011613}}
*Lifetime Risk for Development of Atrial Fibrillation, Circulation. 2004;110:1042–1046, {{doi|10.1161/01.CIR.0000140263.20897.42}}
*Residual Lifetime Risk for Developing Hypertension in Middle-aged Women and Men, JAMA. 2002;287(8):1003-1010, {{doi|10.1001/jama.287.8.1003}}
